items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: I believe Wilbur Swetman used to have an act, he'd play two clarinets at once

ctx.x: Now, Bessier, he used that because he used to make a whole lot of things, he'd make you make an immediate chicken or something, you see. Well, he, and some other things he used to make. Comes from the lip. From the lips. Mm-hmm.

That's using his lips. Very controlling the lip. Well, somebody told me once, I believe Wilbur Swetman used to have an act, he'd play two clarinets at once, and then Sidney, he'd take his clarinet and he'd take one piece off at a time, you know, the bell. I used to do that, too. Yeah, and finally end up with the mouthpiece. Yeah, I used to do that, too. How long did you stay in Chicago with that band?
How long I stayed in Chicago? I was then the race ride. I was then. Oh, the 1919 race ride. Oh, yeah, I was then.
